author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: In the OneLogin admin portal, go to Developers > Webhooks > New Webhook > Event Webhook for Log Management. Set Format to SIEM (NDJSON), the Listener URL to the HTTP Ingest URL, and a custom header Authorization: Bearer <HTTP Ingest key>, so no bridge is needed. Use NDJSON: the JSON Array format puts a whole batch on one line, which HTTP Ingest reads as one record, and those lines stay unclaimed. OneLogin documents the event fields but not the NDJSON line itself; these parsers expect one event object per line and read both the webhook's uuid and event_timestamp and the Events API's id and created_at. Sign-ins, sign-outs, failed sign-ins, OTP failures, lockouts and password changes go to Auth by event_type_id; every other event type goes to CloudAudit with its name from OneLogin's event types list. OneLogin turns the webhook off after about 12 hours of failed deliveries. Samples follow the webhook payload on OneLogin's events webhooks page with made-up values. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (116 of 116 fields matched the emulator), and the parent's confirm string, which starts with ^, picked the same events there and left the JSON array line alone. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent. No built-in parser claimed these events in 9 Run Tests.
